name: Đạp xe đón bình minh
notes: A ride out to meet the sunrise, played by the shared couple (templates/_models: Grab3D's Casual Man and Casual Woman, CC0, animated with Quaternius's Universal Animation Library; see docs/models/README.md). Everything else is built in code: an old blue bicycle sized for them (a long seat post, a tall stem) with spinning spoked wheels, a wicker basket, a bell, a back rack and a lamp; her house front with a window that lights and a door that opens; a cobbled street, its lamp and a sleeping street painted behind; a terraced hill that pops up out of the card with a road winding up it; a page that paints the sky at night, at first light and at sunrise, far mountains, the sun and its rays, and a city in mist that rises at the top; birds. Stop 1: deep blue before dawn, he rides in and rings the bell under her window; her window lights, she comes out, pulls her collar close against the cold and hops sideways onto the back rack; the note tucked in the basket flutters into her hands and opens with the card's first words (slot note1). Stop 2: the street folds away and the hill pops up; they set off up the winding road, he stands on the pedals and wobbles to a stall, she hops off and pushes him from beside the back wheel, laughing, while the stars fade and the sky pales; at the bend she hops back on and the road sign springs up and flips round to the second words (slot note2). Stop 3: round the bend and up to the top, where the city rises out of the mist below and the sun comes up in gold; they turn round for a photo, the flash pops and the print flies up into the card's photo with its caption (slot caption). Stop 4: he goes down on one knee and opens a ring box, she covers her mouth, two birds bring a banner with the last words (slot note3), she cheers, he jumps up and they hug and swing round among petals. The next tap opens the letter. The act is the shared templates/_acts/lovestory.js; this card's own moves are in story.js, its world in scenery.js, the bicycle and props in bike.js, the reaches (feet on the pedals, hands on the grips) and the paper in cast.js.
